Governance & Safety

What you can and can't do with Copilot. The rules are simpler than you think.

TL;DR — The Three Rules

  • No customer data in prompts (names, deals, PII)
  • No proprietary code in unapproved tools
  • Review before sharing — AI output is a draft, not a final

Why Enterprise Copilot is Different

Microsoft 365 Copilot (the version you access through your work account) has enterprise-grade data protection:

  • Your prompts aren't used to train models. What you type stays in your tenant.
  • Data stays within your compliance boundary. Same protections as other M365 data.
  • Outputs inherit permissions. If you can't access a file, Copilot can't either.

This is different from consumer ChatGPT or free Copilot. Enterprise Copilot is designed for work use — that's why we're using it.

What You CAN Do

✓ Approved Uses

  • Draft internal documents (briefs, emails, presentations)
  • Summarize meetings and long documents
  • Brainstorm ideas and outlines
  • Research public information (market trends, competitors)
  • Edit and improve your own writing
  • Generate templates and frameworks
  • Analyze data you have legitimate access to
  • Prepare for meetings and calls

What You CANNOT Do

✗ Prohibited Uses

  • Input customer names, deal details, or account information
  • Share personal data (employee info, contact details, PII)
  • Paste proprietary source code
  • Input confidential financial data or M&A information
  • Use AI output as-is for external communications without review
  • Make claims about product capabilities based solely on AI output
  • Bypass security or compliance controls

Use Caution With

⚠ Proceed Carefully

  • Competitive intelligence: Verify claims independently. AI can hallucinate competitor features.
  • Legal/compliance topics: Get human review before acting on AI legal advice.
  • Pricing and contracts: AI doesn't know current pricing. Verify with official sources.
  • Customer-facing content: Always review and fact-check before publishing.
  • Technical specifications: Cross-reference with documentation.

The Review Principle

AI Output = First Draft

Treat every Copilot response as a starting point, not a final answer. You are responsible for the accuracy, appropriateness, and quality of anything you share externally. Copilot helps you work faster — it doesn't replace your judgment.

Before Sharing AI-Assisted Work

  1. Fact-check any specific claims, statistics, or product details
  2. Verify that tone and messaging align with brand guidelines
  3. Confirm you haven't inadvertently included confidential information
  4. Read it aloud — does it sound like something you'd actually say?

Common Questions

Can I paste a customer email into Copilot?

Avoid it. Even with enterprise protections, customer communications may contain sensitive information. Summarize the situation in your own words instead of pasting verbatim.

Can I use Copilot for competitive research?

Yes, but verify independently. Copilot may have outdated information or hallucinate features. Use it to generate questions and frameworks, then verify with primary sources.

Can I share that I used AI to create something?

Generally yes, internally. For external content, use judgment — a blog post assisted by AI is fine, but implying AI-generated content is original research isn't.

What if I accidentally input something I shouldn't have?

Don't panic. With enterprise Copilot, the data isn't used for training. But do be more careful going forward, and report to IT if you believe there's a compliance issue.

Can I use external AI tools like ChatGPT?

Check the approved tool list. Some external tools are allowed with restrictions; others are prohibited. When in doubt, use enterprise-approved alternatives.

When to Escalate

Contact IT or your manager if:

  • You're unsure whether a use case is approved
  • You accidentally input sensitive data
  • Copilot produces output that seems to include confidential information from other sources
  • You discover a potential security or compliance issue

The Golden Rule

If you wouldn't put it in an email to a colleague, don't put it in a Copilot prompt. Same judgment, same caution, same professionalism.
